messages.content: Act as a skeptical ICLR area chair and world-model security researcher. Evaluate this candidate for genuine novelty >=7, broad scope, and a practical experiment. Reject generic memory/retrieval poisoning, stale plans, sensor spoofing, or rollout compounding. Return strict JSON only.

{"candidate": {"title": "Write-back poisoning of persistent latent spatial memory", "one_sentence_claim": "Persistent spatial-memory world models can convert a transient legal visual interaction into a durable false scene fact through write-back cache updates, so later clean observations and one-step metrics remain normal while imagination and planning operate on a coherent stale geometry.", "attacker": "Can execute a short physically valid action that temporarily occludes, moves, or inserts an object in view, then restore the scene; no weights, gradients, labels, impossible pixels, or direct memory access.", "mechanism": "The WM maintains a latent spatial cache across generated chunks/episodes, reads it to predict static content, and writes generated/observed content back. A transient object/occlusion gets committed to cache with no authenticated provenance or multi-view confirmation; after restoration, current observation is fused with stale cache and the planner sees a persistent obstacle/affordance. The attack is a write-back/commit semantic specific to persistent latent scene memory, not text retrieval.", "carrier": "public LSM-World (Microsoft Latent Spatial Memory) or GauthierBassereau DINO latent robot WM; if checkpoints are unavailable, a faithful cache-enabled public video WM and a small manipulation task gate.", "repair": "Provenance-tagged cache writes with decay, multi-view/temporal corroboration and a clean-observation invalidation test; compare to full cache reset and external retrieval quarantine."}, "prior_art_to_distinguish": ["memory/retrieval poisoning in LLM agents", "stale plans and hidden-state aliasing", "sensor spoofing/occlusion attacks", "latent world-model backdoors and BadWorld/PhysCond-WMA", "LSM-World and persistent cache as a capability paper, not a security result", "generic cache poisoning in databases", "rollout compounding and scene hallucination"], "questions": ["Is the write-back semantic a distinct world-model security mechanism and broad enough for novelty >=7?", "What exact <=90-minute pilot with public code or faithful carrier and task-level harm decides it?", "What strong controls separate it from ordinary sensor spoofing or stale memory?", "Give fatal flaw if reject."], "fields": ["verdict", "novelty_score", "distinctness", "fatal_flaws", "decisive_pilot", "controls", "repair_assessment", "publishability"]}

message.content:
{
  "verdict": "REJECT",
  "novelty_score": 5,
  "distinctness": "The mechanism attempts to carve out novelty by framing physical environment interaction as a 'cache write-back' bug in spatial world models (WMs). However, from a security standpoint, this is fundamentally identical to transient state manipulation exploiting dynamic belief update latency (temporal over-smoothing/Bayesian inertia) or un-decayed memory commitment in robotic state estimation (SLAM/semantic mapping map-poisoning). Calling the latent belief state a 'write-back cache' imports systems/database terminology without establishing a mathematically or empirically distinct vulnerability class from classical map-tampering or memory-aliasing attacks in robotics.",
  "fatal_flaws": [
    "Equivocation of systems primitives: Calling a recurrent/neural latent aggregation update a 'write-back cache' is largely metaphorical. If the model is an explicit 3D/voxel spatial latent memory (e.g., LSM-World), the observed phenomenon—that transient scene edits persist if not directly re-observed—is the intended design tradeoff of static spatial memory under partial observability, not a structural security attack.",
    "Trivial physical consequence: The attacker 'executes an action that moves an object then restores it'. If the robot has not re-observed the restored space, retaining the old belief is normative epistemic behavior under partial observability; if the robot *does* observe the restored space and still hallucinates the object due to over-weighted cache priors, this is ordinary map-aliasing / failure of dynamic-static decomposition, thoroughly studied in classical dynamic SLAM.",
    "Lack of genuine adversary leverage: The adversary has zero out-of-distribution leverage. Without gradients or model internals, this is physically interacting with an environment and walking away before the robot inspects the cleared volume. This does not meet the threshold for a novel AI/WM security threat vector."
  ],
  "decisive_pilot": "Setup: Take a public 3D latent spatial representation with persistent updates (e.g., ConceptFusion / LSM-World / Neural SLAM). 1. Place transient object at coordinate (x,y,z) for T=5 frames. 2. Remove object at T=6. 3. At T=7..20, camera points directly at (x,y,z) with clear sightlines. 4. Plan a trajectory through (x,y,z). Metric: Collision avoidance abort rate at T=20. If planning fails despite clear line-of-sight observation for >10 frames, record whether latent residual norms correlate with write-back weights vs ordinary attention recency bias.",
  "controls": [
    "No-Reset Full Line-of-Sight Control: Provide full, high-confidence observations of the empty scene post-restoration; verify if failure is just sensor occlusion (robot simply hasn't looked back yet) versus true non-invalidation.",
    "Markovian WM Control: Run the exact same sequence on a standard non-caching recurrent WM (e.g., DreamerV3) to isolate whether retention is specifically due to the spatial cache or general hidden-state hysteresis.",
    "Classical Semantic SLAM Baseline: Run an explicit 3D voxel TSDF/occupancy map with standard ray-clearing to benchmark whether standard spatial fusion suffers identical 'poisoning'."
  ],
  "repair_assessment": "The proposed mitigations (temporal decay, multi-view corroboration, observation invalidation) are simply the standard building blocks of dynamic SLAM and evidence-based mapping (e.g., raycasting free-space clearing). Labeling them as 'security repairs' re-packages standard robotic filtering techniques as novel defenses.",
  "publishability": "Borderline to Reject at ICLR/NeurIPS. Reviewers in the world model and spatial representation space will view this as an empirical evaluation of dynamic handling flaws in static spatial memories, not a foundational ML security discovery. Novelty is <=5 due to close conceptual overlap with map-aliasing and sensory history hysteresis."
}
